//: The trusted core: the modules a reader has to trust before handing this
package a page, and the evidence that nothing else needs that trust.
A module is in the core because it holds a capability the page's owner
would ask about: it reads a message from another window, sends a request
with the visitor's cookies, creates the Trusted Types policy, or writes a
value from the wire into an attribute. The primitives those modules defer
to (the escape helpers, the URL check) are in with them: the sanitizer is
only as good as `isSafeUrl`. Modules that hold a capability but stay
outside are listed under `outsideCore` with the reason each one stays
there; a module that holds one and is listed nowhere fails the gate.
rules.ts` holds every module to the capabilities written here. Numbers
are the exact current measurement, no headroom, as in complexity-budget.json.

lines.why: Measured on 2026-09-11, `wc -l` over the eight modules: 386 + 95 + 202 + 68 + 443 + 68 + 48 + 44. A thousand lines is about what one reader holds in one sitting and was the size this core set out to be; this is not it, so the number is a finding, not a target met. What makes it large is not a second responsibility: 133 of the sanitizer's 443 lines are the allow-lists a reader has to read anyway (which tags, which attributes), and about 130 of the bus's 386 are the queue that commits token verdicts in arrival order (ADR 0004) — moving either into a file of its own would leave the reader the same lines in two places. 2026-09-10 the measurement was 1 393 (1 087 without blank and comment lines). 2026-09-11 (Z28): 1 354, after the core's own mutation run showed which lines no test could reach — the merger's redundant abort-signal check, its unreachable collection-slug fallback and the `try { encodeURIComponent }` probes (the one encoding call that builds the path refuses a lone surrogate by itself), the bus's generation checks that the next boundary repeats, its `sendReady` early return, the unreachable `attachedTarget` guard in the source check and the array-with-compaction queue (now a linked list), the escape helpers' empty-string fast paths, the validator's empty check before trimming and the guard `isExternalHttpUrl` implied by its own patterns, and the sanitizer's `insertBefore` loop (now `replaceWith`). `binding-writer.ts` (196 lines) was the obvious ninth candidate; it is outside because it holds no capability — its two exits are `applyAttributeBinding` and a renderer, both held by the gates below — and `docs/audit.md` reads it first after the core for that reason. 2026-09-14 (2.0.1): 1 356. LP0409 said the 1.x `compat` policy kept `name`, which it never did; the sanitizer now asks whether `compat` would have kept it before reporting, one condition on the line that already reported and two comment lines saying why (sanitizer.ts 443 → 445; 1 032 lines without blank and comment lines, unchanged). 2026-09-17 (2.0.2): 1 364. The document `setSanitizerDocument()` supplies moved from a module variable to a registry symbol on the realm, because every package entry is its own bundle with its own copy of this module, and a document set through the root never reached `lexicalToHtml` from `/lexical`, which then returned unsanitised HTML on the server (sanitizer.ts 445 → 453: the symbol, its three-line slot type, and three comment lines saying why). 2026-09-17 (2.0.3): 1 383. The Trusted Types policy moved from two module variables to a registry symbol on the realm for the same reason as the sanitizer's document: a page's `trusted-types` directive allows the name once, so the second bundle on a page (`/lexical` beside the runtime) was refused its own policy and wrote strings, and `setTrustedTypesPolicy()` reached only the entry it was called through (trusted-types.ts 68 → 87: the symbol, its slot type, the accessor and its realm type, and five comment lines saying why). 2026-09-19 (M3, the XSS corpus): 1 391. A parsed element's `is` value is immutable and the serialiser writes it back after the attribute is removed, so the re-parse of sanitised markup upgraded the element to the page's customised built-in of that name; the attribute is emptied instead (sanitizer.ts 453 → 461: the branch and four comment lines saying why).

dependencies.src/core/diagnostics.ts: Wraps a consumer's logger so a diagnostic that throws cannot become a second failure; 38 lines, no capability.
dependencies.src/core/protocol-version.ts: The protocol version constant the `ready` handshake announces, and the capability table read off the wire (ADR 0010); the bus takes only the constant.
dependencies.src/core/thenable.ts: Assimilates a thenable a synchronous callback returned, so a rejected promise from consumer code does not surface as unhandled; 14 lines.
dependencies.src/schema/parser.ts: Validates `fieldSchemaJSON` entry by entry; a malformed entry is dropped and a throw becomes an empty schema. It decides which renderer a field gets, never what is written.
dependencies.src/security/sanitizer-report.ts: LP0409, the once-per-name warning that the strict sanitizer removed an attribute the 1.x default kept. A report, never a behaviour: the attribute stays removed whether or not the warning prints.

src/client/preview-focus.ts.why: The admin-side reporter for reveal tier 2: posts `{ type, field }` to the preview window at its exact origin, never `'*'`. It runs in the admin, not in the page, and carries a field name, never a value.

src/core/loader.ts.why: The static-delivery bootstrap: one `<script>` whose `src` and `integrity` are build-time constants the generator prepends. Nothing from the page or the wire reaches the URL.

src/core/strategy-runner.ts.why: Morphs a fragment the page's own server rendered into its boundary, parsed into a `<template>` first. Sanitising it would strip the page's own legitimate markup; the sink inventory records it as `trusted-origin`.

src/core/structural-applier.ts.why: Parses an item the sanitizer already cleaned into a `<template>` so it can be adopted; `sanitised` in the sink inventory, and inert twice over.

src/field-types/array.ts.why: Renderer; feeds `trustedHtml()` from `sanitizeHtmlWithPolicy()` and nothing else, per site in the sink inventory.

src/field-types/html.ts.why: Renderer; feeds `trustedHtml()` from `sanitizeHtmlWithPolicy()` and nothing else, per site in the sink inventory.

src/field-types/rich-text.ts.why: Renderer; every site feeds `trustedHtml()` a string the sanitizer produced with the instance's policy, including the one that parses a sanitised string into a detached clone.

src/field-types/text.ts.why:
Renderer; feeds `trustedHtml()` from `escapeAndLinebreak()`, which escapes before it inserts `
`; `escaped` in the sink inventory.

src/field-types/upload.ts.why: Renderer; builds one `<a>` from `escapeHtmlAttribute()` and `escapeHtml()` around a URL that passed `isSafeUrl`; `escaped` in the sink inventory.

src/fragment/handler.ts.why: POST to the page's own fragment endpoint with `credentials: 'same-origin'`; the JSON that comes back is validated before any of it reaches a boundary (ADR 0011).

src/fragment/route.ts.why: GET of the page's own route, same-origin, `cache: 'no-store'`; the HTML is parsed by `DOMParser` into an inert document, then morphed. The server that answers is the one that rendered the page.

src/plugins/built-in/document-save.ts.why: Opt-in plugin: on a document event it POSTs to the revalidation URL the consumer configured, or reloads the page. Neither runs unless the page author registered it.

src/security/preview-session.ts.why: Server-side: forwards exactly one named cookie to `<serverURL>/api/<users>/me`. Never in a page; the browser runtime does not contain it.

src/server/preview.ts.why: Server-side draft read through the REST API, with the headers the authorized context carries. Never in a page.

src/doctor/probe.ts.why: `pll doctor`, a maintainer tool run from a shell against a deployment; redirects are reported, not followed, and the body is capped.
